assets.label: export transfer pumps
assets.service: tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family

control_failures.control_label: availability and testing of fixed fire protection
alarm, muster and accounting for people

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: uncontrolled movement of P-7113 during start-up after maintenance

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was lost time injury, with 1 person injured and 4 days lost.

defences.finding: Control FIXED_FIRE_SYSTEM_AVAILABILITY: the availability and testing of fixed fire protection had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control MUSTER_AND_ACCOUNTING: the alarm, muster and accounting for people was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the availability and testing of fixed fire protection on P-7113, M-7113 and PT-7113 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
Restore the alarm, muster and accounting for people on P-7113, M-7113 and PT-7113 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in mustering and rescuing, specifically deploying an emergency response team. P-7113 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during start-up after maintenance while the availability and testing of fixed fire protection had degraded below its design intent. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 4 January 2014 an incident occurred on P-7113, M-7113 and PT-7113 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during start-up after maintenance, releasing chemical energy held as hydrocarbon.
